articles.title: Leaked Hope Florida grand jury report says state ‘misappropriated' funds
articles.standfirst: The report didn’t find enough to pursue criminal charges against anyone.
articles.summary: The report didn’t find enough to pursue criminal charges against anyone.
articles.body:
The report didn’t find enough to pursue criminal charges against anyone.

A state grand jury report found Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis' administration "misappropriated" funds by diverting Medicaid money to a nonprofit, eventually ending up in political committees supporting the governor’s agenda. But the report didn’t find enough to pursue criminal charges against anyone.

The report was first obtained and published by CBS Miami on Wednesday evening. It found $10 million from a total $67 million settlement in 2024 between Florida and Centene Corp., a vendor for the state’s Medicaid program, was sent to the Hope Florida Foundation, the charity arm of an initiative helmed by First Lady Casey DeSantis.

The money was then split equally between two nonprofit groups - Secure Florida’s Future and Save Our Society From Drugs.

Days later a large chunk of that money, $8.5 million, was given from the two groups to Keep Florida Clean, a political action committee staffed by James Uthmeier, who was DeSantis’ chief of staff at the time. DeSantis later appointed Uthmeier to be Florida Attorney General.

Then Keep Florida Clean sent $9 million to the Republican Party of Florida and another $1.23 million to the Florida Freedom Fund, another political committee chaired by Uthmeier.

The committee was dedicated to opposing two measures on the November 2024 ballot. One would’ve installed a right to an abortion in the state constitution, the other would’ve legalized recreational marijuana. Both measures failed to get the 60 percent support required to pass.

The grand jury report found Uthmeier “was in a position of authority over those involved in settling with Centene,” the report says, and witnesses identified him as having involvement in directing the money after it went to Hope Florida. But no witness would identify who specifically directed the money to Hope Florida.

The attorney general’s office did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

The grand jury could not find sufficient evidence to charge anyone criminally, as “nobody will take responsibility for deciding the $10 million of taxpayer money would go to Hope Florida.”

“Virtually everyone involved is a lawyer and acted on the advice of other lawyers,” the report says. “We recognize that this would be an impediment to criminal prosecution. While we can't prove who is responsible, we can plainly see that taxpayer money was misused for political purposes and we would like to see changes made to prevent this from happening again.”

In a social media post, Alex Lanfranconi, communications director for DeSantis, called the CBS Miami story about the grand jury report a “baseless smear” that has been “debunked over and over again.”

“In fact, if any confidential grand jury report was leaked to the press, that’s the only crime committed here,” he wrote on X.

The report also named Ashley Moody, who was attorney general at the time, and said the investigation found Moody “authorized” the settlement agreement with Centene, which included the money that would be transferred to the Hope Florida Foundation. Moody was later appointed to the U.S. Senate by DeSantis.

Moody and Uthmeier are up for reelection in November.

The grand jury investigation into the Medicaid settlement funds began after Rep. Alex Andrade, a Pensacola Republican who chaired the House Health Care Budget Subcommittee, started to look into the matter during the 2025 legislative session.

During the House probe, Andrade, an attorney, accused Uthmeier and Jeff Aaron, a lawyer representing the foundation with close ties to the DeSantis administration, of violating the law with the settlement and the foundation’s subsequent grants.

Andrade declined to comment for this story.

Last October, months after confirming there was an open investigation into the settlement, State Attorney Jack Campbell issued subpoenas for witnesses to appear before the grand jury, but the results of the grand jury investigation had remained hidden from the public until Wednesday, when published by CBS Miami.

For months, Uthmeier, DeSantis and other Republican leaders dismissed questions about the investigation. Hours before the CBS Miami story was published, DeSantis called the scandal a “hoax.”

Democrats fired back Wednesday evening, with Sen. Tracie Davis of Jacksonville, who is in line to be Senate Democratic Leader after the November elections, calling the report’s findings “an egregious abuse of power.”

“The report asked the legislature to make sure that our laws are strong enough to prevent corruption and ensure transparency of public funds,” Davis said in a statement. “To that end, I plan to file legislation in the upcoming legislative session to prevent this type of outrageous abuse from ever happening again.”

Jacksonville Rep. Angie Nixon, the Democratic candidate running against Moody for U.S. Senate, called on Moody to resign for her role in the Hope Florida scandal.

“None of this is leadership. None of this shows good judgment. None of this shows courage,” Nixon said in a statement. “She has broken the public trust, and she must resign immediately.”

articles.title: ‘Everything is covered in ash’: Indonesia wildfires leave people in crisis
articles.summary: Fires severely impacting people’s health in West Kalimantan, with pregnant women and children particularly vulnerable.
articles.body:
Kubu Raya, Indonesia – As wildfires burn across Indonesia, forcing schools to close and thousands to seek medical treatment for exposure to thick haze and ash, locals in West Kalimantan say the situation is more serious than it has been in years.

“I have lived here for 15 years … I have never experienced a fire like this before. This is the first time something like this has happened,” Salma, a resident of Kubu Raya, tells Al Jazeera.

For nearly two weeks in the area, she said, fires grew and spread.

“I was scared, I was afraid that I would be burned by such a big fire. So I evacuated,” Salma said, adding that the fire “almost burned everything”.

“If the firefighters had not come quickly, my house would have burned down, too.”

Volunteer firefighter Anas Dwi Wahyu Kurniawan says the situation is “very serious”, telling Al Jazeera that the fires this year are similar in scale to those that took place in 2016.

Wildfires have been burning for more than a month, and blazes continue to spread through the hot spots of Sumatra, Kalimantan, Sulawesi, Java, and Papua, as emergency crews battle the flames.

On Tuesday, President Prabowo Subianto said the government had deployed dozens of helicopters, aircraft, water pumps, and thousands of personnel to battle the blazes.

Indonesia’s Health Ministry says 3.4 million people are at risk of respiratory infections due to exposure, adding that it had distributed more than 260,000 face masks to residents of the hardest-hit areas.

In Kabu Raya and other parts of West Kalimantan, emergency crews say they are grappling with difficult conditions as fires spread quickly through the dried-up peatland.

They are also grappling with water shortages and haze hampering visibility.

“From what I have experienced, it is much worse compared to previous years,” said Dwi Wahyu Kurniawan.

He added that he and other volunteers “face limitations in terms of personal protective equipment, as well as emergency equipment such as portable oxygen and other supplies”, severely complicating their task of putting out the fires.

“With water sources far away and inadequate equipment,” he said, “I think the situation will continue for some time unless there is a change in the weather.”

The fires are having a severe impact on people’s health, with doctors saying that many patients are arriving with persistent coughs.

“On a daily basis, most of the complaints from patients here are coughing and sore throats, or what we call throat inflammation. Every day, between 50 and 70 people come in,” said Dr Muhammad Arief Trihapsoro, at the Sungai Durian Health Clinic.

Conditions like bronchitis are a major concern, as well as the long-term impacts of prolonged exposure to air pollution, including a heightened risk of stroke and heart disease.

Medics say pregnant women and children are among the most vulnerable.

Many parents have had to bring their children to health clinics and hospitals several times as symptoms associated with the fires keep reappearing.

“I brought both of my children [to the health clinic]. They have stomachaches, fever, coughs and runny noses,” Siti Zahra, a mother of two, told Al Jazeera.

“They have been sick for two days, but before that they were also sick for three days, then they got sick again. So, in this one month, they have been sick three times because of the smoke, ash, drought and fires.”

Zahra said that it’s impossible to avoid the ash, as it even invades their home.

“Everything is covered in ash, so I have to sweep every day. Not just once a day – even after I sweep, there is more ash in the back of the house. I sweep it up, and then there is more. I’m getting tired of sweeping.”

She is so concerned about her children’s health that she doesn’t even allow them to go outside.

“I’m also afraid to go outside. I don’t dare take the children out, so they just stay at home,” she said, adding that her children refuse to wear the protective masks she gave them, so “when we are here [at the health clinic], I force them to wear masks so they are not exposed to even more haze and ash”.

“I’m very worried that this [haze and ash] will have a long-term impact on their health,” Zahra said. “In the long term, their health could become even worse.”

articles.title: Parliament may be reconvened, hints Rijiju, brings delimitation bill in focus
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Keeping the opposition on edge by dropping indications about the possibility of Parliament being reconvened, parliamentary affairs minister.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Keeping the opposition on edge by dropping indications about the possibility of Parliament being reconvened, parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju has said that Prime Minister Narendra Modi had made a commitment to women for speedy implementation of the women’s reservation law and govt is working in that direction.Citing Rijiju’s comments to India Today, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge Thursday shot off a letter to the PM, demanding an all-party meeting to discuss govt’s proposal for delimitation before calling a special session of Parliament, as “indicated” by the union minister.Though Rijiju made no categorical comment about an immediate session to take up the constitutional amendment bill to implement the law from 2029 with a 50% increase in Lok Sabha seats, he said Parliament has been reconvened in the past after a session was not prorogued.The monsoon session, which ended on Aug 13, has not been prorogued yet. “Already, the PM has made a clear-cut commitment to women of the nation that women’s reservation and the commitment given by Parliament to women will be implemented. Based on that, we are working,” Rijiju said.The Congress president said Rijiju’s comment ties in with the delay in the prorogation of the monsoon session of Parliament.“This is an issue that has enormous significance for the country. Please do not again try and bulldoze things as you attempted on April 16-17, 2026,” Kharge wrote to Modi. The April 16-17 reference is to the discussion and voting on the bill in Lok Sabha in which the Opposition voted down govt’s proposed legislation.Kharge told the PM that his party is clear that the current strength of the Lok Sabha (543 MPs) and the respective share of the states in it should be frozen for 25 years. Congress also wants that women’s reservation should be implemented from the 2029 Lok Sabha elections as per Parliament’s existing strength.The Congress president reminded the Prime Minister that he had also written to him on July 16 seeking an all-party meeting to discuss govt’s proposals for delimitation and that the parties be given enough time to study them before they are introduced in Parliament.The leader of opposition in Rajya Sabha told Modi that before calling the special session, he should call an all-party meeting and give political parties and state govts adequate time to study the proposals.In his Independence Day address to the nation, Modi had said, “I pray to and urge all political parties to come forward and acknowledge the power of women. Let’s step forward to uphold their dignity and ensure that our mothers and sisters get 33% representation in assemblies and Lok Sabha as soon as possible.”Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: US Postal Service says mail-in ballot restrictions now in effect
articles.summary: The US Supreme Court ruled in favor of changes backed by President Donald Trump, but new challenges have been filed.
articles.body:
New restrictions on how the United States Postal Service will handle mail-in ballots are now in effect, even as challenges in court to the measures touted by US President Donald Trump continue.

The Postal Service announcement on Thursday comes as states are preparing to send out millions of ballots to voters through the mail ahead of US midterm elections scheduled across the US on November 3.

“The government subsequently received such relief from those injunctions, meaning the injunctions no longer preclude the implementation of the Rule for November 3, 2026 or any earlier federal election,” the independent federal agency said.

The new procedures mean the agency would compile lists of eligible voters using input from US states and only deliver ballots to individuals who are on those lists.

On Monday, the US Supreme Court cleared the way for the new measures by ruling in favour of the Trump administration. Other court challenges to the rules continue, however, including a fresh case filed in a federal court in the US state of Massachusetts on Wednesday by 24 states. State attorneys-general argue the measures are unconstitutional and would also inflict “significant, imminent, and irreparable harm” on states by imposing “new and burdensome mail voting requirements” just before the November elections.

Voting by mail has long been a favourite target for Trump, who has claimed that it breeds fraud despite strong evidence to the contrary and his own use of the voting method. President Trump has claimed states have not done an adequate job in verifying who sends in mail-in ballots, and that those registered to vote meet requirements like being US citizens.

In March, Trump signed an executive order calling on his administration to create lists of eligible voters and the Postal Service to deliver mail-in ballots only to those on those lists.

The Postal Service had come up with regulations on how it would handle mail-in ballots based on that directive, but put its implementation on hold as Democratic officials in dozens of states, along with voting rights advocacy groups, lodged legal challenges in federal courts.

Monday’s Supreme Court case, which has a 6-3 conservative majority, ruled in the Trump administration’s favor in one of those key challenges: Officials from dozens of states had sued to block the presidential order, arguing that the US Constitution gives states and Congress the power to run elections and that Trump’s changes could lead to chaos and partisan abuse.

The Trump administration then appealed to the Supreme Court on procedural grounds in late July after a judge ruled in the officials’ favour for the midterms, arguing that the states sued too soon. The court did not decide on the constitutionality of the order.

Voting by mail has become increasingly popular with voters of both Republican and Democratic parties, accounting for about 30 percent of ballots cast during the 2024 presidential election, according to federal data. Despite claims by Trump about problems with mail-in voting, experts have found it to be secure. A 2025 Brookings Institution study found only about four cases of fraud out of every 10 million mail ballots cast.

articles.title: Govt plans to engage third-party auditor to inspect NHs, e-ways
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: As concerns rise over deficiencies in quality of work and premature failures in expressways and NH projects, the road transport ministry wi.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: As concerns rise over deficiencies in quality of work and premature failures in expressways and NH projects, the road transport ministry will engage a third-party inspection agency (TPIA) for inspection and examination of around 5,000 km of expressways and highway stretches from the start of construction until project completion. The agency will initially be engaged for a period of three years.TOI has learnt that the ministry has decided to onboard Engineers India Ltd (EIL), an engineering consultancy under the petroleum ministry. The agency will audit mainly expressways, six-lane and four-lane national highways.At present, third-party quality audits are conducted through independent quality auditors, who are mostly retired govt engineers empanelled by NHAI and other agencies. EIL had earlier carried out the task of third-party quality check during the construction of the Golden Quadrilateral, the country’s first flagship highway development programme under the then PM Atal Bihari Vajpayee.In recent years, increased instances of deficiencies in NH projects have become a cause of concern, as these have attracted criticism from the public.Officials said the latest move was needed given the poor feedback from the independent auditors. The agency will be tasked with inspecting 770 km of expressways, 2,200km of six-lane highways, and another 1,000km each of NHs that are four and two lanes.Earlier this year, PMO had directed the road transport ministry to introduce independent third-party audits to ensure high-quality work.As per the plan, Engineers India Ltd’s scope will be “limited to inspection and examination” of quality of work by verifying the compliance of technical specifications and standards as per contract.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: PM Modi to meet Russia's Putin on SCO meeting sidelines
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: PM Narendra Modi will have a bilateral meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin on the margins of the upcoming SCO summit in Bishkek, .
articles.body: NEW DELHI: PM Narendra Modi will have a bilateral meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin on the margins of the upcoming SCO summit in Bishkek, said govt while announcing Modi’s two-nation central Asia tour to Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan that begins Saturday. The summit meeting of the Eurasian bloc will take place on Aug 31-Sept 1.In Bishkek, Modi will also come face to face with Chinese President Xi Jinping before he hosts him for the Brics summit here on Sept 12-13. Modi’s other bilateral engagements are still being finalised.Modi’s bilateral with Putin, the first since the Russian President visited India in Dec 2025 for the annual summit, will follow external affairs minister S Jaishankar’s visit to Moscow this week for a meeting of the 27th India-Russia Inter-Governmental Commission on Trade, Economic, Scientific, Technological and Cultural Cooperation during which he also called on Putin.While discussing trade and investment, energy and nuclear cooperation, Putin assured Jaishankar of continued supply of fertilisers, saying Russia is doing everything to help Indian farmers. Jaishankar told him Modi is looking forward to hosting him for the Brics summit in Sept.This year’s summit marks the 25th anniversary of the SCO, of which India has been a full member since 2017 along with Pakistan. With Islamabad watching, India is again likely to remind the grouping that the original SCO mandate was to fight terrorism, extremism and separatism.“The Prime Minister will address the summit where he will highlight India’s priorities of security, connectivity and opportunity at the forum. He will also hold bilateral meets with SCO leaders on the sidelines of the summit,” said MEA, adding that Modi will also attend the opening ceremony of the 6th World Nomad Games, a celebration of the rich cultural heritage of central Asia, in Kyrgyzstan.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Clean-up of illegal Kidlington waste supersite costs £6m
articles.summary: The bill for clearing the dump in Oxfordshire has been covered by taxpayers.
articles.body:
The clear-up of one of England's largest illegal waste tips has been completed - landing taxpayers with a £6m bill.

The government has vowed to recoup the clearance costs for the Kidlington dump in Oxfordshire - and seven other sites - from the criminals responsible.

In 2025, around 22,000 tonnes of domestic and commercial rubbish was dumped at the spot, between the River Cherwell and the A34. It is one of nearly 30 so-called "supersites" first uncovered by a BBC investigation .

The government, which launched a crackdown on waste crime last week, said it would do more to force criminals to pay for clean-up operations by confiscating their money and assets.

But figures obtained by the BBC show that, in the past five years, the Environment Agency has so far managed to claw back just over £7m from waste criminals using Proceeds of Crime Act (Poca) confiscation orders.

At the same time, the agency says waste crime costs the economy £1bn a year.

Campaigners have labelled the amount taken from convicted criminals as "derisory" while the Country Land and Business Association (CLA), which represents rural landowners, asked: "Where is the deterrent?"

The amount paid by criminals so far was revealed by an Environmental Information Regulations (EIR) request to the Environment Agency by the BBC.

It shows there have been 66 confiscation orders between January 2021 and March 2026, totalling £7.3m.

Fourteen orders have yet to be fully paid, leaving around £1.4m still to be recovered.

The figures cover those larger illegal sites for which the Environment Agency is responsible, and do not include confiscation orders for smaller fly-tipping offences, which fall under the remit of local authorities.

Baroness Sheehan, who chairs the House of Lords environment and climate change committee, said the figures obtained by the BBC showed "consistent, decisive enforcement" was lacking.

"With clean-up costs at sites such as Kidlington far exceeding these sums, and enforcement still lagging, the taxpayer continues to foot the bill," the Liberal Dem peer said.

"The Environment Agency must do more to secure and enforce confiscation orders against those responsible, so criminals pay - not communities."

As well as the work at the Kidlington site, the Environment Agency has also stepped in to clear a supersite at Hoads Wood, near Ashford in Kent .

The cost of these two clearances alone has been budgeted at £20m by the Environment Agency - although the Kidlington project has come in under the original £7.3m contract.

The government estimates that 20% of waste in England is illegally managed.

In the Waste Crime Action Plan , launched under Keir Starmer's administration, the government said the Environment Agency would step in "on an exceptional basis to clear sites where that waste presents an untenable risk to the public and the environment".

Private landowners whose land is used for illegal waste dumping are normally expected to pay for the clear-up.

Last week, Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced a nationwide crackdown on waste crime and plans to clean up three more of the largest illegal tips in England.

In total, six supersites have been earmarked to be cleared using public money, but they will be assessed first. They are:

Power Station Road - Isle of Sheppey, Kent

Alan Ramsbottom Way - Hyndburn, Lancashire

Worthing Road - Sheffield, South Yorkshire

Bolton House Road - Bickershaw, Greater Manchester

Environment secretary Dame Angela Eagle said: "After years of waste crime being allowed to fester, we are taking decisive action.

"By putting more officers on the frontline and using drones to catch offenders in the act, we're putting the criminal gangs on notice that there is nowhere left to hide."

But many more illegal supersites remain - and it is not known if or when they will be cleared up, and who will be made to pay.

This includes one supersite in the countryside of Over, Gloucestershire, which Charlie Coats, chairman of Highnam Parish Council, is calling for the Environment Agency to also deal with.

He told the BBC that the amount of money taken from waste criminals was "derisory" and added: "It acts as absolutely no deterrent whatsoever because the income that they can derive from this dwarfs anything by way of any fine."

Gavin Lane, president of the CLA, which represents around 28,000 landowners, farmers and rural businesses across England and Wales - who are often left paying the cost of clean-up - also called for more to be done to make the criminals foot the bill.

"The punishment has to be real: seize their vehicles, recover the money they owe and make waste crime a losing business," he said.

The Environment Agency told the BBC that some of the unpaid confiscation orders were outstanding "because they are still within the six-month payment period allowed for settlement" and the failure to pay was a matter for the courts.

It added that more money could still be seized if further information is uncovered about the offenders' assets.

Four men have so far been arrested in connection with the illegal waste tip at Kidlington. All have since been released while the investigation continues.

articles.title: Ratko Mladić, 'Butcher of Bosnia' convicted of genocide, dies at 84
articles.summary: Ratko Mladić, the notorious Bosnian Serb general convicted of genocide and war crimes, has died at age 84 in a Hague prison hospital while serving a life sentence.
articles.body: Ratko Mladić, the Bosnian Serb warlord general who oversaw wartime atrocities as he led forces that carried out the worst massacre in Europe since World War II, has died. He was 84. Mladić, known as the "Butcher of Bosnia," died at a hospital in The Hague, Netherlands, U.N. court officials said. He had been in custody since 2011 after years on the run for war crimes committed during the wars in the former Yugoslavia in the 1990s. In 2017, he was sentenced to life in prison. EX-PHILIPPINE PRESIDENT DUTERTE TO FACE TRIAL ON CRIMES AGAINST HUMANITY CHARGES Mladić was one of the most notorious figures in the conflict that left more than 100,000 people dead and displaced more than a million others. Under his command, Bosnian Serb troops took control of large swaths of Bosnia and Herzegovina and laid siege to the capital of Sarajevo and other cities. His forces detained non-Serb civilians and enemy soldiers in concentration camps and systematically slaughtered prisoners. Despite the charges levied against him, Mladić never showed remorse. In court, he yelled at the judges when he was sentenced. "He was murdered there, in those dungeons," Janko Seslija, a former Bosnian Serb soldier, told The Associated Press. "I feel sorry for Gen. Mladić. He was an honorable man, honorable soldier and commander." A former Communist-era military officer, Mladić sided with the Serbs as Yugoslavia broke apart and disintegrated into war. He led a Serb insurgency in Croatia before taking over the Bosnian Serb army, according to The AP. Among the horrors Mladić was charged with was the 1995 slaughter of up to 8,000 Muslim men and boys in Srebrenica, which was supposed to be a safe zone guarded by Dutch peacekeepers. articles.title: I used to live in a quiet area - now there's a data centre overlooking my garden
articles.summary: With the number of UK data centres set to rise by a fifth, some communities are concerned about the impact.
articles.body:
Overlooking the garden of Amanda Young's family home is a data centre.

"It used to be a nice, quiet area," said Amanda, who lives near to one of the large buildings in Newport.

"But with more data centres coming in, we kind of don't know what they're going to bring with them."

Data centres are buildings full of powerful computers used to run digital services, from online banking to movie streaming.

The number of data centres across the UK is on the rise as the growth in artificial intelligence (AI) increases the need for processing power.

The UK government classifies data centres as critical national infrastructure and, according to recent Senedd research, "most jobs in the UK" are now reliant on them.

But concerns have been raised about the large amounts of resources data centres require - including electricity, grid capacity and water - as well as the impact on the local communities where they are built.

Once fully operational, the Vantage Data Center Campus in Newport, south Wales, will include three centres over 46 acres.

Amanda, whose home overlooks the site, said her biggest concern was "the noise, the visual impact and whether it will affect house prices" in her local area.

"Whichever window you look out, you can see it," she said.

"When you're sitting in the lounge, you can actually see it there."

Anthony, who lives near Amanda, said the construction of the data centre "takes away the peace from the neighbourhood" because of the noise and the extra traffic.

A spokesperson for Vantage Data Center said they were "committed to being a good neighbour", adding they "work closely with local authorities" to "manage construction activity, including traffic, noise and lighting" as well as incorporating "measures designed to protect the local environment".

Newport City Council said, when considering planning applications, it worked to "ensure that the impacts are considered acceptable in terms of biodiversity, light, noise and construction traffic".

In Cardiff, campaigners are concerned about proposals for a data centre campus in Llanrumney, on the site of the Cardiff East Park & Ride that takes passengers to the University Hospital of Wales.

"The park-and-ride is so important," said Sue Elias, who uses the service and has been campaigning against the proposal with the residents' union Acorn.

Elias said she understood the need to build data centres but said "there should be a pause" to consider the most responsible sites.

"They shouldn't just be put up and then worry about the consequences afterwards."

Cardiff and Vale University Health Board (CVUHB) said the park and ride was an "essential transport link", adding that it was "committed to identifying a suitable and convenient alternative location".

Data centres could pay hundreds of millions in deposits for power demands

'I can't drink the water' - life next to a US data centre

The campaigners are also concerned about the potential impact on the environment.

"The data centre planned would be an environmental nightmare both for the wildlife and the local residents," said Lizzie Bailey, who lives locally.

"This will be a temporary disruption with the construction but then a permanent disruption because of the diesel generators, the noises, the cooling fans, things like that."

Curtis Hall Ltd, the company behind the plans, said the development would "not put a strain on the energy grid or water infrastructure".

The company added: "The data centre's water and drainage requirements have been developed in consultation with Welsh Water and any connection to the public network requires their agreement.

"This ensures our data centre can be accommodated without impacting the supply of water to residents' homes."

It said a "detailed noise impact assessment" concluded the site "won't have an adverse impact on the nearest homes in terms of noise, including at night".

Cardiff Council said the proposal was being considered, and that "as with all planning applications, the proposal will be assessed against relevant planning policies and material planning considerations".

The council encouraged people with "comments, concerns or views" to submit them through the consultation process.

There are currently 568 data centres listed in the UK, according to the data centre map .

Research suggests that number is set to increase by almost a fifth with nine proposed in Wales.

A Senedd Research document recently outlined the opportunities that data centres could bring, including "jobs, investment, skills development and support for innovation".

But it also noted the "significant resource and policy questions they raise", including electricity demand, grid capacity, water use, land requirements, biodiversity and impacts on local communities.

Ofgem said the amount of electricity being requested by data centre projects seeking to connect to the grid had risen from 41GW to 125GW in the past year, reflecting a sharp increase in demand.

Water UK, the trade association for the UK's water industry, estimated that data centres used approximately 6.6 million litres of water each day - the equivalent used by 20,000 average homes.

By some analyses, the UK is already the third-largest nation for data centres behind the US and Germany.

Prof Alan Brown from the University of Exeter, the author of Making AI Work for Britain , said authorities should be "a lot more engaged" with communities about the construction of data centres.

"If that gets bypassed, then of course local residents are going to worry that they're getting all of the pain and none of the benefit."

He said when people understood the implications of a data centre and what it meant for them, "they're more willing to be more flexible".

"I think right now, there's a lack of communication around that."

The environmental group Friends of the Earth is calling for a UK-wide pause on all new data centres.

"We're asking for that pause until there are clear rules set out on how much energy and water data centres can use, to make sure they're not sucking up our much-needed renewables and our clean water," said Kierra Box, from the group.

"We need an idea of how now, and in the future governments are going to determine the individual and the joint impact of all these data centres on the environment, on communities, on nature."

But tech founder Mark John said the development of data centres and AI (artificial intelligence) infrastructure had offered "an opportunity for Wales" to "reimagine itself".

"AI, data and data centres are going to be at the forefront of the new Industrial Revolution," said John, co-founder of Tramshed Tech.

"This could be the new frontier technology, in the same way that coal and steel were at the forefront of industrial transformation."

John said he recently travelled to Seattle where a "very senior figure" in the tech industry had outlined "that because of AI, the whole way we live our lives is going to change more in the next six months than it has in the previous 10 years".

"That sort of brought it home to me - like it or loathe it, we have to live with it and come to terms with it."

John said data centres would unlock AI capability in Wales, adding that "if we haven't got data centres, we haven't got access to that AI".

"I won't call them a necessary evil but they are a means to an end, if you like."

The UK government said many newer data centres were "already using advanced cooling systems that significantly reduce water consumption, and the data centre sector operates under a Climate Change Agreement to encourage greater uptake of energy efficiency measures amongst operators".

It added: "Data centre planning applications are required to consider the impact on communities and the environment.

"We will enable the development of data centres by building unprecedented amounts of clean power, while our AI Growth Zones support data centre development in areas with access to clean energy."

The Welsh government said it recognised that data centres were "energy intensive", and that it was important for new developments to make use of technologies to minimise energy and resource consumption.

"Any proposed data centre development remains subject to the existing planning system and environmental regulation, with robust checks and balances in place to ensure that environmental and community impacts are properly considered before consent is granted," it added.

"Investment in data centres has the potential to create new economic opportunities and support skilled employment, while strengthening Wales' attractiveness as a leading destination for advanced digital investment."

articles.title: GTA 6 extended look: What we know after Netflix preview
articles.summary: The official look at the blockbuster video game leaves fans and critics impressed.
articles.body:
After more than 18 months since the last official glimpse of Grand Theft Auto 6, developer Rockstar has shown fans a 26-minute preview of the upcoming blockbuster video game.

Its "extended look" debuted on Netflix, six hours before going live on YouTube, and was the first chance players have had to see detailed footage of the title in action.

The montage, with no commentary or explanatory captions, showed off improved graphics, detailed environments and a selection of car-chases and shoot-outs from the sequel.

The broadcast followed a week of unauthorised gameplay leaks , which the developer said it had been "heartbreaking" to see shared online.

After it got its chance to show the version of GTA 6 it wanted the world to see, here are some things we learned, and some things we still don't know.

The extended look spent a long time showcasing the relationship between protagonists Jason Duval and Lucia Camino, the couple at the centre of GTA 6's "Bonnie and Clyde" story.

In a preview published on website IGN , the developers said the characters' story - and the way it unfolds - can be affected by the player's actions, although they can "opt out" of developing the pair's bond if they want.

The Netflix preview didn't show this playing out in detail, but did show the ability to change control between the two characters at different points.

In one segment, Jason was seen lowering Lucia from a window as they escaped from a drug bust in a block of apartments.

A similar switching system was used in Grand Theft Auto 5, which had three playable main characters.

Praise for GTA 6's graphics was more or less universal, with characters displaying photorealistic faces and lifelike movements.

Fans were also impressed by the detailed locations on show, which included the interiors of apartments, rooftop bars and sleazy underground clubs.

The preview also showcased the various environments of Leonida, the fictional, Florida-inspired US state where GTA 6 is set.

The range of different body shapes and sizes among background characters - something rarely seen in video games - was also highlighted by many players watching online.

Journalist Ryan McCaffrey said GTA 6 "might be the best-looking game I've ever seen".

The impressive visual fidelity has been attributed to the amount of time Rockstar has spent working on the game, and its budget, which is thought to be among the most expensive in video game history.

While GTA 6 appears to break new ground in terms of visuals and scale, it is still, at its heart, a Grand Theft Auto game.

During the preview, viewers saw the armed heists, car chases and criminal underworld scenes that have become a trademark of the series.

Satirical swipes at US culture, darkly comic interactions between characters and a huge range of optional side activities were all present once again.

And Rockstar appears to have expanded on features it introduced in its last major release, 2018 hit Red Dead Redemption 2, such as an "honour" system that affects the player's reputation among other characters.

Fans of the series, which is estimated to have sold half a billion copies since it launched in 1997, will have been thrilled to see it.

Rockstar had already stated that GTA 6 will be a "single-player experience" on launch, leaving fans to assume a follow-up to the incredibly successful online element of its previous games would come later.

The Netflix preview was dedicated to showing off the story and gameplay, and was not necessarily expected to highlight any new multiplayer features.

Although the launch of the game on 19 November is widely expected to be the biggest of all time, the long-term success of GTA 6 will be judged on how well Rockstar converts players to any new online mode.

GTA online, which also launched after the release of GTA 5, remains one of the most-played games in the world, and is thought to have generated billions of dollars for Rockstar.

The previous game in the series, GTA 5, also broke records when it came out in 2013 and has sold more than 200 million copies since.

Two official trailers for the sixth game have almost 500 million combined views on YouTube, and the Netflix "extended look" on Thursday is being marketed as an event by the streaming service.

Next month the company is due to appear at an employment tribunal in Scotland to defend itself against claims it illegally sacked a group of ex-employees for trying to form a union .

It strongly denies the accusations, and says the workers were fired on the grounds of gross misconduct.

articles.title: Meet Neil Gilson, the Devon swimmer who became the first person to swim Switzerland’s 10 largest lakes in a gruelling 230-mile challenge
articles.summary: UK News: Meet Neil Gilson, the 40-year-old former international swimmer from Devon who has completed an extraordinary endurance challenge, swimming across Swit.
articles.body: Meet Neil Gilson, the 40-year-old former international swimmer from Devon who has completed an extraordinary endurance challenge, swimming across Switzerland’s 10 largest lakes over two summers. Together, the crossings covered about 230 miles (370km), culminating in a gruelling 45-mile swim across Lac Léman, also known as Lake Geneva, that lasted just over 22 hours. Gilson’s achievement, known as the Legend of the Lakes challenge, marks the first time anyone has completed the feat. His final swim was particularly emotional, with his children, Lily and Jack, joining him for the last 200 metres. But Gilson’s story is about more than endurance swimming. He began the challenge partly to raise awareness of PANS and PANDAS, conditions that affected his son Jack as a young child.Neil Gilson’s journey from elite swimmer to Swiss lake endurance challengerGilson’s extraordinary swimming career did not begin with Switzerland’s enormous lakes. He was once ranked second in Britain for the 1,500-metre freestyle before eventually moving away from competitive racing and towards endurance swimming. His transition opened the door to increasingly ambitious open-water challenges, culminating in his decision to attempt all 10 of Switzerland’s largest lakes. Gilson trained extensively in a leisure-centre pool, the sea off the North Devon coast and the gym before taking on the challenge. His preparation was necessary because lake swimming brought its own set of unpredictable difficulties. Gilson told The Guardian that lakes could be more demanding than the sea, with wind producing choppy water and sudden walls of cold water. The BBC had also followed Gilson earlier in his challenge, documenting his progress and the extraordinary scale of his ambition before he completed the final lake.How did Neil Gilson swim 230 miles across Switzerland’s biggest lakes?Gilson spent two summers working through Switzerland’s 10 largest lakes, eventually accumulating approximately 230 miles of open-water swimming. The challenge required him to contend with dramatically different conditions across the lakes, from cold Alpine water to wind and strong currents. His previous experience on Lac Léman proved important. In 2024, Gilson crossed the lake in 22 hours and nine minutes, setting a world record at the time. Rather than stopping there, he decided to use that experience as the foundation for the much larger Legend of the Lakes challenge. The final crossing alone covered approximately 45 miles and lasted more than 22 hours. The challenge was far from straightforward. Gilson said Lake Maggiore, which involved a swim of around 40 miles, almost broke him after the water proved colder than expected. He had to increase his swimming pace to keep his core temperature up, using more energy than planned. Lake Thun also became difficult as the physical strain and pressure of completing the challenge accumulated.Why was Gilson’s final 22-hour Lake Geneva swim so difficult?The final crossing of Lac Léman became one of the hardest tests of Gilson’s endurance. He began swimming on Tuesday morning and did not finish until Wednesday lunchtime, spending more than 22 hours in the water. Around 18 hours into the crossing, he considered stopping as a strong current made the night-time section particularly difficult. Gilson told The Guardian, “It was so tough in the night, the current was strong.” He said he came “really close to stopping”, but the knowledge that his family was waiting at the finish kept him moving. His support crew travelled alongside him by boat, supplying coffee and encouragement during the marathon swim. Although he narrowly failed to beat his own Lac Léman world record, that was no longer the main goal. Completing all 10 lakes was the achievement he had spent two summers pursuing. As he emerged from the water, he had completed roughly 370km of swimming and became the first person to accomplish the Legend of the Lakes challenge.What motivated Neil Gilson to take on the challenge?Behind Gilson’s extraordinary sporting achievement is a deeply personal reason. His son Jack developed PANDAS after contracting tonsillitis when he was 2-3 years old. Gilson has used his endurance challenges to raise awareness of PANS and PANDAS, neuropsychiatric conditions associated with a range of behavioural, psychological and movement-related symptoms. Gilson told The Guardian that Jack had been a healthy child before suddenly developing severe symptoms, including aggression, OCD, tics and intense fear. The experience inspired his campaign to improve awareness of conditions that he believes remain underdiagnosed. That personal motivation was especially visible at the end of the final swim. His 12-year-old daughter Lily and 10-year-old Jack entered the water and swam the final 200 metres alongside their father. Gilson said there were “tears in my goggles” as they joined him, explaining that he had imagined that moment throughout the challenge. For Gilson, therefore, the 10 lakes were never simply 230 miles of open water. They represented a test of endurance, a family journey and a way to draw attention to a cause that has shaped his life. He now expects Guinness World Records to recognise the achievement officially, although other ultra-swimmers may eventually attempt to complete the same challenge faster.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Haiti police confront public frustration after deadly gang attack kills 47
articles.summary: The attack in Kenscoff, a community where crime had been declining, has raised questions about Haiti’s security.
articles.body:
Haiti’s national police has faced growing scrutiny over its failure to stem violent attacks by armed criminal groups, which killed 47 people and kidnapped more than 50 last weekend.

Police spokesperson Garry Desrosiers held a news conference on Thursday, taking questions from a handful of reporters.

He offered few details about how the police plan to respond to the August 23 mass kidnapping, considered one of the largest such incidents in the country’s recent history.

“We cannot talk about any plans,” Desrosiers said.

The attack on the community of Kenscoff, located in the hills outside of the capital city of Port-au-Prince, has underscored the continued influence of powerful gangs in the country.

Hundreds of people fled the attack. Desrosiers said that police are working to return them home.

One gang leader has threatened to execute all the hostages if any gang members are killed as police work to gain control over Kenscoff.

Asked whether police had gathered any intelligence before the attack, Desrosiers offered sparse comments, saying authorities have been working to find information.

He added that the police believe one gang leader has threatened an assault on Tabarre, a neighbourhood in the capital that is home to the United States embassy.

“I’m not in a position to give you detailed information,” Desrosiers said.

The attack on Kenscoff comes as authorities in Haiti seek to reclaim control of the capital city. The United Nations estimates that the community has suffered about a dozen gang attacks since last year.

But violence had been dropping in the area. Between January and August, the nonprofit conflict monitor Armed Conflict Location and Event Data found that the crackdown had lowered violence in Kenscoff by 66 percent compared with a year ago.

Still, the UN has warned that gang-related violence is “spreading geographically even as the authorities’ anti-gang campaign intensifies in Port-au-Prince”.

The international body has estimated that more than 3,050 people have been killed across the country between January and June alone.

“These figures show that the population continues to bear an unacceptable toll from violence,” the UN’s top representative in Haiti, Carlos Ruiz Massieu, said in a statement on Tuesday.

Armed groups have acquired growing influence in Haiti since the assassination of former President Jovenel Moise in 2021, which left a power vacuum in the country’s government.

No national elections have been held in the years since, and the last elected senators saw their terms expire in 2023 .

Haitian officials have repeatedly attempted to schedule a new vote, only to postpone the elections due to security concerns and other factors. Currently, a general election is scheduled for December.

Armed groups in the country have pointed to the political and economic instability as justification for the violence.

Currently, an estimated 70 percent of Port-au-Prince is under gang control. Clashes have displaced more than 1.5 million people across the country.

In April, the first members of a UN-backed Gang Suppression Force arrived in Haiti with the aim of dismantling organised violence in the country.

It was also designed to relieve a smaller multinational security mission led by Kenya that struggled with a lack of funding and support.

UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres has expressed optimism about the arrival of the force’s members.

“Their deployment offers a real opportunity to curb violence and restore the authority of the state,” he said after visiting their base in June.

But critics have argued that international efforts have had little success so far. Such missions have also drawn uncomfortable comparisons to previous foreign interventions in Haiti, many of which have faced accusations of rights abuses.

Haitian police have also struggled with allegations of corruption, incompetence and, in some cases, collaboration with armed groups.

Vladimir Paraison, head of Haiti’s national police, did not attend Thursday’s news conference but has defended the police from criticism since the Kenscoff attack.

He has indicated that an investigation is underway to probe whether the violence was enabled by “complicity or negligence”.

articles.title: Newspaper headlines: 'Town gripped by fear' and 'Nepal death toll climbs'
articles.summary: Several papers focus on the violence unfolding in Middlesbrough, described by the Mirror as a town "under seige".
articles.body:
The devastation in Nepal is pictured across many of the front pages. The Daily Mail reports on the British families desperately trying to contact missing relatives, after what's described as a "tsunami from the sky" .

The Times says a nurse from Kent is among the missing , while the Sussex businessman, Pramod Poudel, tells the Daily Telegraph from Gatwick Airport he is travelling back to his Nepalese home village to try to find his wife, mother, uncle and brother.

The Guardian focuses on warnings that there could be further flooding , with a newly-formed lake now at risk of bursting. According to the Financial Times, the disaster is a "brutal reminder of the growing risks to people in the Himalayas", which is "deeply vulnerable to climate change".

"Under siege" is the headline in the Daily Mirror, which leads on the deployment of hundreds of additional police officers in Middlesbrough - where it says "residents are living in fear" because of an "alleged gangland turf war".

One resident tells the Daily Express: "It seems like the whole town has gone crazy" . Another, quoted in the Sun, says: "It's scary, you wonder what's going to happen next". The paper's front page asks how a UK town could become a "war zone".

The i Paper r eports that guards at the Chinese embassy in London have been caught threatening protesters with banned electro-shock batons. The paper says the incident has sparked a diplomatic row, with the government warning Beijing that it will not tolerate any attempts "to coerce, intimidate, harass or harm" people on UK soil. The Chinese embassy has been contacted for comment.

Sources tell the Mirror that the Home Office is "actively" reassessing whether Prince Harry and his family should have taxpayer-funded security. Since moving to the US, the Duke of Sussex has paid for his own protection. But insiders say now that he is moving back to the UK, "the goalposts have moved".

And the Telegraph declares that people over 40 are "the last generation of regular drinkers". A study by 'Our Future Health' suggests those in their forties are 52% more likely than younger people to exceed government alcohol recommendations.

articles.title: Syria’s president appoints ex-commander of Kurdish-led SDF as advisor
articles.summary: Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa appoints Mazloum Abdi as presidential advisor, three days after dissolution of SDF.
articles.body:
Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa has appointed Mazloum Abdi, leader of the now-dissolved Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF), as a presidential advisor.

Al-Sharaa issued Decree No 164, appointing Abdi as “as an advisor to the Presidency of the Republic” on Thursday, the Syrian state news agency Sana reported.

The move comes three days after Abdi announced the dissolution of the SDF and the completion of its integration with the Syrian military.

Abdi is the most senior of several Kurdish figures appointed to state posts. Another commander was made assistant defence minister for the eastern region earlier this year.

The advisory role is a lesser position than one offered in January, when al-Sharaa proposed making Abdi deputy defence minister and nominating him as governor of Hasakah province, in order to restore state control over the SDF-controlled provincial capital.

Al-Sharaa and Abdi first agreed to fold the SDF into the central government in March 2025. That deal made little progress before its year-end deadline, spurring state forces to battle into the northeast in January, taking the cities of Raqqa and Deir Az Zor from the SDF.

A ceasefire that ended the fighting placed Raqqa, Deir Az Zor and Hasakah under central government control and committed the SDF to join the defence and interior ministries under a 14-point plan.

One Kurdish-led force has yet to be absorbed. The YPJ , the SDF’s women’s units, asked to join the defence ministry but were told the army’s structure has no units for women.

Alongside the military track, al-Sharaa issued a decree in January recognising Kurdish as a national language and restoring citizenship to Syria Kurds, the first formal recognition of Kurdish rights since Syria’s independence in 1946.

The SDF was the largest force still outside the army, and its dissolution leaves Damascus with formal authority over almost all Syrian territory. Reunifying the country has been al-Sharaa’s central promise since former Syrian leader Bashar al-Assad was overthrown in December 2024.

articles.title: Jacob Elordi on why The Dog Stars had him asking 'What am I missing?' in life
articles.summary: Sir Ridley Scott's post-apocalyptic epic explores the feeling of hope in a pandemic-riddled world.
articles.body:
A devastating pandemic, environmental destruction and a depleted society reduced to anarchy are the themes at play in Sir Ridley Scott's latest film The Dog Stars.

Based on Peter Heller's 2012 novel of the same name, the stars of the sci-fi film say they hope its themes will makes viewers question the parts of their lives they take for granted.

Jacob Elordi stars as the lead character, Hig, a former mechanic turned pilot, who spends his days flying over Colorado with his dog Jasper, searching for a better life.

He tells the BBC the film portrays "the human condition", with the characters living in "the apocalypse" but "still looking for something else and hoping for something else".

The film, which features a star-studded cast of Guy Pearce, Margaret Qualley and Josh Brolin, is set in the 2030s, where only those immune from a deadly flu remain alive.

It immediately draw parallels with the Covid pandemic with its aerial shots of abandoned cities and Hig's constant search for resources like food and medicine.

Elordi, who received his first Oscar nomination earlier this year for Frankenstein, says "there were a few moments I remember looking around [on set] and thinking it's strange to be doing this make-believe, when the reality is just behind us and just in front of us".

He says a dystopian future like the one portrayed in the film is "frightening to think about" but "it's something we have to examine and remember, because we are on the cusp of these realities".

The 29-year-old also says he resonates with his character's struggle to be content with life.

"Everything is sweet for us - we're able to walk around on the street, go to the shops, go to the park, have dinner with each other and we still go to bed and think 'What else is there?', 'What am I missing?', 'What's wrong?' and nothing is".

This is also true for his co-star, Mare of Easttown and Memento star Pearce, who plays Pops, the survivor who meets Hig after emergency-landing his plane near his home.

Pearce says the way the film highlights "this world we take for granted" is "pertinent" adding: "You can go to the supermarket and get food and wake up with your family - a lot of people even to this day don't live like that, so I am absolutely aware of [my] privilege".

The film's anarchical vibe is also portrayed through its environment, with scenes of scorched earth that resemble the images many of us have seen in places affected by wildfires.

This is personal to both Pearce, who previously worked with Sir Ridley on Prometheus in 2012, and Elordi. Both were raised in areas of Australia that have been recently damaged by natural disasters.

"I've been in Australia when there's been serious bushfires," says Pearce, whose home state of Victoria was damaged earlier this year.

"All round the world now there's just more and more effects of climate change so it's pretty terrifying that a lot of those things are not far away," he says.

Elordi, who hails from Brisbane, is a little more hopeful about the future of the climate in the context of the film - pointing to other parts where you can see lush expanses of greenery.

"Something interesting and not to be missed is the idea of regrowth - that in this abyss, four or five years after the worst day ever for human beings, the trees are full, the grass is thick and the flowers are growing out of the decay".

He says this provides "a note of hope" and "idea of redemption", adding that this relates to real life through wildfires because "when a wildfire destroys an entire coast, inevitably the nature and the earth rebuilds and regrows".

'Difference between surviving and thriving'

Early reviews of the film have been mixed, with The Guardian's Benjamin Lee three-star review describing it as a "limp and lethargic film that only briefly fascinates in pushing us to wonder what anyone was really hoping this would end up being".

David Rooney at The Hollywood Reporter is slightly more positive, noting that the film is "muted but never dull" and an "appealingly mellow watch".

But in a two-star review , Empire's Helen O'Hara says the film "tries to examine the difference between surviving and thriving" but "doesn't seem entirely convinced of its own answers".

The film got three stars from Tim Robey at The Telegraph, who notes the film's "action interludes are more nonsensical than scary" and "provide momentary dumb fun when Scott's campfire apocalypse needs waking up".

Sir Ridley says the film was inspired by Covid, but also the original book's context, having been written in the wake of the 2008 global financial crisis.

"If you put those two together you've got a great combination of chaos," he notes, adding: "If you have chaos, you get panic and anarchy and away you go".

He also says he thought a lot about his upbringing when building the film's virus-stricken world.

"I was a war baby so I can remember incendiary bombs dropping on me and we'd have to shelter under the stairs. So the Second World War to me was apocalyptic".

Elordi notes that he is "afraid of large movies and things packed with action set pieces" but was reassured by Sir Ridley as "the master of these kinds of films".

"I would have done any movie he sent through for me to make, it's a privilege to get to work with a pioneer of our industry in my lifetime - it's kind of unfathomable," he adds.

The Dog Stars is out in UK cinemas on 28 August.

articles.title: US charges 81 in Puerto Rico gang case, as Trump cartel crackdown continues
articles.summary: The arrests are part of a federal task force initiative targeting criminal gangs and transnational organisations.
articles.body:
The United States Department of Justice has indicted 81 people over alleged drug and weapons violations, as part of a crackdown on a Puerto Rican criminal group called Los Baja Deo or LBD.

Attorney General Todd Blanche announced the charges on Thursday during a visit to Puerto Rico. A day earlier, the US Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and Puerto Rico Police Department arrested 70 of the defendants.

“Let this be a warning to those that are terrorizing our communities,” Blanche said in a statement.

“Our Homeland Security Task Forces around the country are unified to end the presence of criminal cartels, foreign gangs, and transnational criminal organizations throughout the United States.”

The mass indictment arrives as part of an effort under US President Donald Trump to weaken and dismantle criminal organisations across the Western Hemisphere.

His administration has called the hemisphere “ America’s neighborhood “. It has pledged to take hardline, and sometimes lethal, action in the region against those it considers to be “narco-terrorists”, a word it frequently applies to suspected drug-traffickers.

Thursday’s indictment alleges that, starting in 2021, members of LBD began distributing drugs in and around public housing projects and neighbourhoods in Mayaguez, a city in western Puerto Rico.

They are also accused of using the US Postal Service to send drugs from the island, which is a US territory. Among the substances allegedly trafficked were heroin, fentanyl, cocaine and marijuana.

According to the Justice Department, LBD distributed at least 340kg of fentanyl or fentanyl-laced narcotics and at least 2,200kg of cocaine in the last five years. The operation generated more than $49m in proceeds.

The indictment also accuses members of using violence, like murders and kidnappings, to protect their drug-trafficking conspiracy.

The defendants facing drug-related charges alone face the possibility of at least 10 years in prison. Those accused of both drug and firearms charges could face a minimum of 15 years. The maximum penalty in both cases is life imprisonment, if the defendants are convicted.

The Justice Department also said it is seeking to seize $49.7m in assets as part of the criminal case.

In Thursday’s announcement, FBI Director Kash Patel praised law enforcement work in the case as “outstanding” and touted the large-scale arrests as a blow to drug trafficking into the US mainland.

“These arrests disrupted one of western Puerto Rico’s most violent drug‑trafficking organisations, dismantled its leadership and distribution networks, and cut off yet another key pipeline of dealt drugs flowing into our country,” Patel said.

The arrests were conducted as part of Trump’s Homeland Security Task Force, which was established by executive order in 2025 to target cartels, foreign gangs and transnational criminal organisations.

The task force network has over 9,000 federal agents, task force officers and analysts.

Since taking office for a second term, Trump has sought to beef up government efforts against drug traffickers.

Early in his term, his administration began designating Latin American criminal groups as “foreign terrorist organisations “, allowing US authorities to pursue those groups under counterterrorism laws.

But critics have warned that such designations have been used to justify extrajudicial killing and other abuses of power.

Since September 2, 2025, for instance, the Trump administration has repeatedly bombed small boats in the Caribbean Sea and eastern Pacific, on the basis that they transported drugs. Some 227 people have been killed in that bombing campaign.

No evidence has been presented in the cases, and the victims’ identities remain largely unknown.

articles.title: Morango cravejado: doce vira tendência e gera filas no interior de SP | G1
articles.standfirst: Sucessor do 'morango do amor', novo doce supera expectativas e confeitaria de São José dos Campos vende 100 unidades em duas horas.
articles.summary: O morango cravejado surge como sucessor do morango do amor e movimenta confeitarias de São José dos Campos com vendas recordes e grandes filas de espera.
articles.body:
Se você está habituado a rolar o feed das redes sociais, pode já ter visto ele por aí. É o morango cravejado, doce que está virando tendência nas redes e ganhando espaço nas vitrines de confeitarias .

Depois do sucesso do morango do amor em 2025, confeiteiros agora apostam nessa nova versão para conquistar clientes. Em São José dos Campos , confeiteiros já registram procura pelo doce. Em uma das confeitarias, houve até fila de espera.

Em uma confeitaria da Zona Leste, de São José 100 unidades foram produzidas para o lançamento e acabaram em menos de duas horas. O sócio-proprietário da Na Divinos Chocolateria, Henrique Bueno, diz que a procura surpreendeu.

"Já superou as expectativas de vendas. Tem até uma fila de espera de pessoas que querem o morango cravejado", afirma.

Já na Zona Norte, a confeiteira Danielle Andrade, da Dani Doces, também decidiu testar a novidade depois de vê-la nas redes.

"A gente fez um teste com 10 morangos e esgotou em uma hora. Depois fizemos mais 60 e também esgotou. Então foram 70 unidades em um dia", conta.

Danielle avalia que o doce ainda está no início da popularização, mas acredita que a procura pode crescer e fazer com que ele permaneça no cardápio nas próximas semanas.

Foto 1: Morango cravejado da Divino's Chocolateria / Foto 2: Morango cravejado da Dani Doces — Foto: Foto 1: Divino's Chocolateria / Foto 2: Dani Doces

O morango cravejado leva uma camada de brigadeiro de chocolate branco ao redor da fruta e cobertura de chocolate branco com pedaços de caramelo . A cobertura crocante dá origem ao nome "cravejado".

Segundo os confeiteiros, os ingredientes aumentam o custo, mas também deixam o doce mais saboroso.

"O morango é um produto na confeitaria que a gente fala que ele é quase nobre mesmo. E usamos o chocolate nobre também. São ingredientes mais caros e acabamos repassando esse valor aos clientes, mas sempre equilibrando custo e qualidade", afirma Henrique.

O sucesso inicial já faz os confeiteiros compararem o cravejado ao fenômeno do morango do amor.

“Como a gente já trabalha com morango e eu gosto muito de chocolate branco, decidi apostar. Acho que pode bater o morango do amor ou ficar até mais famoso.”, diz Danielle.

Para Henrique, o novo doce também pode ajudar nos planos de expansão do negócio.

"Quando o morango do amor chegou, ele fez a gente trocar de carro. E agora o morango cravejado vai ser a mesma coisa, vai ser o investimento pra nossa nova loja", afirma.

Ainda é cedo para saber se o morango cravejado terá a mesma força do morango do amor, mas a velocidade das primeiras vendas indica que o novo doce encontrou espaço entre os consumidores que acompanham as tendências da confeitaria nas redes sociais.

articles.title: Aliança entre milícia e TCP contra o CV é alvo do MPRJ | G1
articles.standfirst: Investigação aponta que grupos historicamente rivais passaram a trocar armas, munições, veículos roubados e apoio logístico. Operação prendeu 2 PMs e 1 traficante nesta quinta (27).
articles.summary: A aliança entre milícia e TCP para combater o CV motivou operação do MPRJ que prendeu policiais por tráfico de armas e apoio logístico no Rio de Janeiro.
articles.body:
Uma investigação do Ministério Público do Rio de Janeiro (MPRJ) revelou uma aliança entre milicianos que atuam na Zona Oeste do Rio e traficantes do Terceiro Comando Puro (TCP) de comunidades da Zona Norte.

Segundo o MP, os grupos, historicamente rivais, passaram a cooperar principalmente por terem um inimigo em comum: o Comando Vermelho (CV).

Conversas obtidas pelos investigadores mostram integrantes dos grupos tratando da parceria e da troca de apoio logístico. Segundo o Grupo de Atuação Especializada de Combate ao Crime Organizado (Gaeco/MPRJ), o esquema envolvia negociação de armas e munições, bloqueadores de sinais e veículos roubados.

A investigação resultou em uma operação nesta quinta-feira (27), que prendeu dois policiais militares e um traficante . Ao todo, 20 pessoas foram denunciadas por crimes como extorsão, homicídio e constituição de milícia privada. Quatro dos denunciados já estavam presos.

A apuração teve início depois da prisão em flagrante de Yuri Guimarães Soares, em novembro de 2023, em Santa Cruz, na Zona Oeste. Yuri estava em um carro com outras duas pessoas. No veículo, foram encontrados fuzis e carregadores.

A análise do celular de Yuri levou os investigadores a conversas que, segundo o MP, indicam que ele funcionava como um elo entre a milícia de Curicica, em Jacarepaguá, e integrantes do TCP que atuam em áreas como os complexos da Maré e da Pedreira.

De acordo com a investigação, os dois grupos mantinham uma aliança estratégica baseada em interesses comuns na disputa territorial contra organizações criminosas rivais, principalmente o Comando Vermelho.

Em uma das conversas, Yuri fala com Osmar Silva de Souza, conhecido como Messi ou Novinho, apontado pela investigação como integrante da milícia.

“O TCP não é inimigo nosso, pelo contrário, é mais de ajudar a gente”, escreveu Yuri, segundo o MP.

Em outra mensagem, ele reforça a estratégia de união contra o CV:

“Nossa guerra é com os [integrantes do] Comando Vermelho. O segredo da vitória é nossa união, irmão.”

Os investigadores também identificaram uma troca de mensagens entre Yuri e Thauan da Silva Menezes, conhecido como Balão e apontado como integrante do TCP.

Segundo o Ministério Público, Balão atua no Complexo da Maré, especialmente na Vila do João, e participa da compra e venda de drogas no atacado.

A investigação afirma ainda que ele atua na negociação de armas de fogo, mantendo contato com fornecedores e compradores, inclusive para a comercialização de fuzis.

Para o MP, as conversas e demais elementos reunidos durante a investigação demonstram que integrantes da milícia e do TCP passaram a cooperar apesar da rivalidade histórica entre os grupos.

Entre os presos na operação desta quinta estão dois policiais militares .

Jorge Anastácio Rodrigues Simões foi encontrado no batalhão onde trabalha, em São Cristóvão, na Zona Norte. Leo Carlos Anjos dos Santos, lotado no batalhão de Botafogo, na Zona Sul, foi preso em casa.

Segundo a denúncia, os dois são suspeitos de fornecer e intermediar a venda de armas e munições destinadas tanto à milícia quanto a traficantes ligados ao TCP.

Um traficante também foi preso na operação.

O Ministério Público denunciou, ao todo, 20 pessoas por crimes como extorsão, homicídio e constituição de milícia privada.

articles.title: Tragédia no Himalaia entra no 3º dia com temor de nova avalanche | G1
articles.standfirst: Equipes usam máquinas e cães farejadores para procurar vítimas sob lama e escombros. Cerca de 1 mil pessoas continuam desaparecidas.
articles.summary: Equipes usam máquinas e cães farejadores para procurar vítimas sob lama e escombros. Cerca de 1 mil pessoas continuam desaparecidas.
articles.body:
As equipes de resgate entraram nesta sexta-feira (28) no terceiro dia de buscas por sobreviventes e corpos após uma avalanche de gelo provocar uma inundação no Nepal e no Tibete. As autoridades temem uma nova avalanche nos próximos dias.

Pelo menos 389 pessoas morreram no Nepal e três no Tibete. Ao todo, cerca de mil continuam desaparecidos nos dois territórios.

Entre os desaparecidos, estão pelo menos 540 estrangeiros, muitos deles turistas, peregrinos e montanhistas que estavam em uma região conhecida por trilhas.

Helicópteros sobrevoam cidades e vales isolados para procurar sobreviventes e levar alimentos e outros suprimentos a milhares de pessoas que ficaram presas em áreas isoladas.

Em terra, equipes usam máquinas pesadas e cães farejadores para procurar vítimas sob a lama e os escombros. Dezenas de corpos foram encontrados longe da área mais atingida, levados pela força da água pelos rios que descem do Himalaia.

Dibga Tamang foi uma das últimas pessoas resgatadas da cidade de Rasuwa, uma das mais atingidas, na quinta-feira (27). Ela e outras três pessoas foram levadas de helicóptero para uma base do Exército.

"Todas as nossas pessoas se foram. Estão mortas. Não tenho ninguém esperando por mim. Tudo e todos se foram. É o fim."

No Tibete, equipes de resgate ainda enfrentavam dificuldades para chegar à região mais atingida da passagem de fronteira de Gyirong, segundo a imprensa estatal chinesa.

Casas destruídas por avalanche no Nepal em 26 de agosto de 2026 — Foto: Navesh Chitrakar/REUTERS

Além das buscas, as autoridades passaram a monitorar lagos formados depois que rios foram bloqueados por rochas e destroços.

No Nepal, um lago formado após o bloqueio do rio Bhotekoshi continua enchendo e corre o risco de se romper.

Na China , autoridades afirmaram que cerca de 3 milhões de metros cúbicos de água devem chegar nos próximos três dias a outro lago bloqueado por destroços. O volume equivale a aproximadamente 1.200 piscinas olímpicas.

Segundo a imprensa estatal chinesa, há um risco elevado de que o lago transborde ou se rompa. O pico da cheia está previsto para 1º de setembro.

"O volume de água continua aumentando, e o risco também", afirmou Zhu Jinfeng, pesquisador do departamento de hidrologia do Ministério dos Recursos Hídricos da China, à emissora estatal CCTV.

articles.title: Macaé e UFRJ firmam parceria para aprimorar tratamento da obesidade | G1
articles.standfirst: Clínica municipal tem cerca de 800 pacientes cadastrados, dos quais aproximadamente 130 fazem tratamento com semaglutida.
articles.summary: Clínica municipal tem cerca de 800 pacientes cadastrados, dos quais aproximadamente 130 fazem tratamento com semaglutida.
articles.body:
A Clínica da Obesidade de Macaé, no Norte Fluminense, formalizou uma parceria com a Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro (UFRJ) para fortalecer o acompanhamento dos pacientes e ampliar a produção de dados científicos sobre os tratamentos oferecidos pela rede municipal.

A unidade recebeu uma visita técnica da vice-reitoria da UFRJ. A clínica abriga o Laboratório de Pesquisa Assistencial em Doenças Crônicas (LASSDOC), vinculado ao curso de Nutrição da universidade.

A parceria permitirá que as experiências e os resultados obtidos durante o acompanhamento dos pacientes contribuam para a produção de conhecimento científico. A integração entre a universidade e o município também busca aprimorar a assistência e desenvolver estratégias voltadas à qualidade de vida da população.

Vice-reitoria da universidade realiza visita técnica à Clínica da Obesidade — Foto: Arquivo Secom

Atualmente, o laboratório acompanha cerca de 40 pacientes submetidos a diferentes tratamentos, como uso de semaglutida, cirurgia bariátrica e implantação de balão intragástrico. São analisados indicadores fisiológicos, antropométricos e clínicos para avaliar os resultados das abordagens adotadas.

A Clínica da Obesidade possui aproximadamente 800 pacientes cadastrados. Desse total, cerca de 130 utilizam semaglutida, princípio ativo presente em algumas das chamadas canetas emagrecedoras.

O tratamento também inclui reeducação alimentar e acompanhamento de uma equipe multidisciplinar formada por nutricionistas, psicólogos, endocrinologistas, cirurgião bariátrico e cardiologista.

Para ter acesso ao serviço, o paciente deve procurar o atendimento de Nutrição da Estratégia Saúde da Família ou da Unidade Básica de Saúde de referência. Após a avaliação, poderá ser encaminhado à Linha de Cuidados de Sobrepeso e Obesidade.

A clínica funciona na Rua Antero Perlingeiro, nº 47, no Centro de Macaé.

A programação começa à tarde com um bate-papo sobre qualificação profissional, seguido por uma palestra internacional on-line com o sociólogo espanhol Manuel Castells, que aborda as relações entre inteligência artificial, comunicação, poder e organização social.
